clue.text: Fake message lately in cryptic form?

parts.note: cod is a British informal adjective for fake or mock, as in a cod accent

indicators.note: lately means at the end, so only the closing letter of the word message is kept

parts.note: the final letter of message

explanation.surface: Someone suspects a recent message is a forgery dressed up in secret writing.
explanation.definitionFit: A cipher or secret system of symbols is a form of writing meant to be hidden from outsiders.

clue.text: Councillor, correct character to get source of funds

parts.note: Cr is the standard abbreviation for councillor
to edit a text is to correct it
a card is an eccentric or amusing character

explanation.surface: A local politician sets about putting things right to raise some money.
explanation.definitionFit: A plastic payment card lets the holder borrow and spend money, so it supplies cash when needed.

clue.text: Masquerade about extremists in sections inside a NI party

indicators.note: inside tells us the preceding letters sit within the party's abbreviation

parts.note: the DUP is the Democratic Unionist Party of Northern Ireland
re means about or concerning

indicators.note: extremists are those at the far ends, so only the first and last letters of sections are used

parts.note: the outer letters of sections

explanation.surface: A political report about a Northern Irish party's internal factions sounds like an exposé of pretence.
explanation.walkthrough: The DUP is Northern Ireland's Democratic Unionist Party; 'sections' looks like party factions but only lends its outer letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To put on a costume and pretend to be someone else is to disguise oneself, a verb sense of masquerade.

clue.text: Most of line teacher prepared is free from trouble

indicators.note: most of means nearly all, so the last letter of line is dropped
prepared means worked up or made ready, so these letters are rearranged into new form

parts.note: line without its final letter
taken as written

explanation.surface: A teacher's carefully prepared lesson plan keeps them out of difficulty.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means no longer under suspicion or in danger, safely out of a difficult situation.

clue.text: Dislike poverty on the outskirts of Lille

parts.note: need is want or poverty

indicators.note: the outskirts of a town are its edges, so only the first and last letters of Lille are kept

parts.note: the outer letters of Lille

explanation.surface: Someone dislikes the deprivation found around the edges of a French city.
explanation.walkthrough: To have the needle is British slang for bearing a grudge, which is why it can stand for dislike.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun, it is British informal for hostility or antagonism between rivals, a grudge felt against someone.

clue.text: School gets stick about a main thoroughfare

parts.note: a high school

indicators.note: about here means going round, so the stick is wrapped around the letter from a

parts.note: a rod is a stick
taken as written

explanation.surface: A school is handed a stick concerning a busy main road.
explanation.definitionFit: A principal public route between towns is the chief road, the opposite of a byway.

clue.text: Impediment left out for lowly member of company?

indicators.note: left out tells us the abbreviation for left is omitted from the word for impediment

parts.note: a clog is an obstruction or impediment
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: An obstacle was ignored when assessing a junior employee of a firm.
explanation.walkthrough: CLOG loses its L.
explanation.definitionFit: A small, replaceable worker in a big organisation is called a cog in the machine, an unimportant part of the whole.

clue.text: Titled figure with estate overlooking country in Ireland previously

parts.note: an earl is a titled nobleman, traditionally holding landed estates

indicators.note: in places the country's letter inside the abbreviation standing for Ireland

parts.note: IR is an abbreviation for Ireland
E is the international vehicle code for Spain

explanation.surface: A nobleman's estate once looked out over the Irish countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'overlooking' means sitting above, so the nobleman comes first. E for Spain is an international vehicle code, a convention worth learning.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something happening at a prior time, before now or before another event.

clue.text: Small part of litter found in bar untouched

indicators.note: found in says the answer is sitting within the run of letters that follows

parts.note: spanning the end of bar and start of untouched

explanation.surface: A tiny bit of rubbish lies untouched in a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Litter' looks like rubbish dropped in a bar; it is a set of newborn animals.
explanation.definitionFit: The weakest and smallest animal born in a litter of piglets or puppies is called this.

clue.text: Possibly sole importance is to get thinner

indicators.note: possibly suggests one of several versions, so the following word is rearranged

parts.note: rearranged
weight means significance or importance

explanation.surface: A dieter whose one priority is to slim down.
explanation.definitionFit: Shedding pounds or kilos makes the body slimmer, so to slim and to drop pounds mean the same.

clue.text: One trailing criminal reportedly noticed repellent sight

parts.note: a private eye is a detective who tails suspects

indicators.note: reportedly means as said by others, so we want a word spoken like the word noticed would be

parts.note: saw means noticed, and in a non-rhotic accent sounds like sore

explanation.surface: A detective shadowing a crook spotted something nasty.
explanation.definitionFit: An ugly building or object that spoils the view is something unpleasant to look at.

clue.text: Noted Soviet from Georgia represented in rag

indicators.note: represented means shown in a different form, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: GA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Georgia
these five letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A famous Soviet citizen from Georgia featured in a tabloid paper.
explanation.walkthrough: Georgia tempts as the Soviet republic, but here it is the American state.
explanation.definitionFit: Yuri Gagarin was the Soviet cosmonaut who became the first human in space in 1961.

clue.text: For example, housing publication

definitions.meaning: first meaning: housing is an example of a political topic of debate
second meaning: a single edition of a magazine or newspaper

explanation.walkthrough: 'Housing' looks like a container signal; it is the example of a topic.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a subject of public concern and also one numbered edition of a periodical.

clue.text: Place to see square, maybe, taken by joint authority

parts.note: Lord's is the London cricket ground, and the square is a cricket field's central pitch area
the hip is a joint

explanation.surface: A venue where a square can be watched is taken over by joint management.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Square' looks like a town square or a stuffy person; it is the strip of pitches at Lord's.
explanation.definitionFit: Lordship means dominion or rule over land and people, the power held by a lord.

clue.text: One not viewed professionally in the main?

definitions.text: One not viewed professionally in the main?

parts.words: One not viewed professionally in the main?
parts.note: surface reading: someone mostly overlooked in their line of work
setter's reading: the main is the sea, and this person works hidden under its surface

explanation.walkthrough: 'In the main' reads as 'mostly', but the main is an old word for the open sea, where an underwater vessel's crew go unseen.
explanation.definitionFit: A sailor serving aboard an underwater naval vessel works out of sight beneath the ocean.

clue.text: Hurry up playing with game on TV, one lacking name

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters are at play, moving freely into a new arrangement
lacking means without, so the letter standing for name is removed

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
N is the abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: Someone is urged to get going while a nameless figure plays a televised game.
explanation.walkthrough: One N is dropped from the eleven letters of game on TV one before the rest are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: The informal command urges someone to be quicker, the same as telling them to hurry.

clue.text: Fall first right away for figure in force

indicators.note: away says to remove, and first right picks the first occurrence of the letter abbreviating right

parts.note: to come a cropper is British slang for to fall heavily
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A tumble first then removes a person from the police.
explanation.walkthrough: CROPPER loses its first R.
explanation.definitionFit: Copper is British slang for a police officer, a member of the police force.

clue.text: Crowd supported end to fine, lively celebration

parts.note: a jam is a crush or crowd
bore is the past tense of bear, to support

indicators.note: end to points to the closing letter of the word fine

parts.note: the last letter of fine

explanation.surface: A crowd backed the end of a fine, festive party.
explanation.definitionFit: A jamboree is a large noisy party or gathering, also a scouts' rally, full of high spirits.

clue.text: Key part arranged around end of revue for comedian

indicators.note: arranged means put in a new order, and around takes the extra letter in among them

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: end of points to the closing letter of revue

parts.note: the last letter of revue

explanation.surface: An important role is set up around the finale of a comedy revue.
explanation.walkthrough: Peter Kay is a popular British stand-up comedian from Bolton, star of Phoenix Nights.
explanation.definitionFit: Peter Kay is a well-known English stand-up and sitcom performer, so a professional funny man.

clue.text: Stock German touring second of conferences is one frequenting meetings?

parts.note: race means stock or breed

indicators.note: touring means travelling round, so the German abbreviation goes around the letter

parts.note: Ger is an abbreviation for German

indicators.note: second of points to the second letter of conferences

parts.note: the second letter of conferences

explanation.surface: A German delegate who tours conferences attends many meetings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Meetings' looks like business conferences; in Britain a race meeting is a day of horse races.
explanation.definitionFit: A regular at the horse races attends race meetings, and the question mark flags the sporting sense.

clue.text: Companion, a type causing hilarity in horse-drawn vehicle

parts.note: CH is Companion of Honour, a British order
taken as written
someone very funny is a riot

explanation.surface: A friend who is a real laugh rides in a carriage.
explanation.definitionFit: A two-wheeled carriage pulled by horses, used in ancient warfare and racing, is a chariot.

clue.text: Light touch shown by popular Australian in film

parts.note: a pat is a gentle touch
in means fashionable or popular
A is an abbreviation for Australian

explanation.surface: A popular Australian actor shows a deft touch in a movie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Film' looks like a movie; it is a thin surface layer.
explanation.definitionFit: A patina is a thin coating or sheen that forms on metal or wood with age, so a surface layer.

clue.text: How one might describe letters briefly

definitions.meaning: first meaning: letters sit together inside a word
second meaning: to put it concisely

explanation.walkthrough: 'Letters' suggests correspondence; here they are the alphabet's characters forming a word.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means summed up concisely, and literally places characters of the alphabet together in one term.

clue.text: Supported by everyone after onset of COVID-19 — like some doctors?

parts.note: on means resting on or supported by

indicators.note: the onset of something is its beginning, so the first letter of COVID-19 is taken

parts.note: the first letter of COVID-19
all means everyone

explanation.surface: Everyone rallied round after the pandemic began, as some doctors did.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' puts ALL behind C.
explanation.definitionFit: Doctors who are available to be summoned to work at short notice outside normal hours are described this way.

clue.text: Heavily criticise article about memorial to the dead?

parts.note: to pan a show is to criticise it harshly
the definite article
on means about, as in a book on birds

explanation.surface: A critic savages a piece of writing about a war memorial.
explanation.definitionFit: A pantheon is a building where a nation's illustrious dead are buried or commemorated, like the one in Paris.

clue.text: Current US prosecutor with influence not half in Western state

indicators.note: not half means half is missing, so the second half of the word for influence is dropped

parts.note: I is the symbol for electric current
a DA is a district attorney
to have a hold over someone is to have influence

explanation.surface: An American prosecutor's influence is waning in the Wild West.
explanation.walkthrough: HOLD loses its second half to leave HO.
explanation.definitionFit: Idaho is a state in the north-western United States, bordering Washington and Montana.

clue.text: Meat cost regularly on reflection is a swindle

indicators.note: a reflection shows things back to front, so the chosen letters are read in the opposite order
regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter of meat cost is taken

parts.note: the first, third, fifth and seventh letters of meat cost

explanation.surface: Looking back, the price charged for meat is a rip-off.
explanation.definitionFit: A scam is a dishonest scheme to cheat people out of money, the same as a fraud or con.

clue.text: Greek character given retreat that's secluded in warm wind

parts.note: chi is a letter of the Greek alphabet
a nook is a secluded corner or retreat

explanation.surface: A Greek gets a secluded hideaway, sheltered in a balmy breeze.
explanation.definitionFit: The chinook is a warm dry wind that blows down the eastern slopes of the Rocky Mountains.

clue.text: Film award namely brought out, something familiar to Redgrave?

indicators.note: brought out means taken out, so the abbreviation for namely is removed from the award

parts.note: the Oscar is the Academy Award for film
sc, short for scilicet, means namely

explanation.surface: A film award goes to a Redgrave, the famous acting family.
explanation.walkthrough: The acting Redgraves (Vanessa, Michael) fit the film award, but this is Sir Steve Redgrave, the British Olympic rowing champion.
explanation.definitionFit: Steve Redgrave won five Olympic golds in rowing, so a blade for propelling a boat was his daily tool.

clue.text: Exotic name taken by singular plant

indicators.note: exotic means strange and foreign, so the word that follows takes an unfamiliar arrangement

parts.note: rearranged
singular means single, one

explanation.surface: An unusual name has been chosen for a rare plant.
explanation.definitionFit: The anemone, or windflower, is a flowering garden plant of the buttercup family.

clue.text: Secure period of time around Thailand to get scooter, maybe

indicators.note: around means encircling, so the word for secure surrounds the letter for Thailand

parts.note: to moor a boat is to secure it
T is the international vehicle code for Thailand
a cycle is a recurring period

explanation.surface: Someone books time travelling round Thailand on a scooter.
explanation.walkthrough: T for Thailand is its international vehicle registration code.
explanation.definitionFit: A scooter is one type of powered two-wheeler, given as an example with the word maybe.

clue.text: Powerful deity representing peace?

wordplay.note: peace is zero noise: O for nothing and din for noise

explanation.surface: A mighty god stands for peace.
explanation.walkthrough: O is a zero, so 'O din' is no noise, which is peace.
explanation.definitionFit: Odin is the chief god of Norse mythology, ruler of Asgard and god of war and wisdom.
